product.name: Example Notes
product.description: A shared notebook for small teams.

hosting.description: {{product.name}} runs in a private network on Amazon Web Services. Every request passes through Cloudflare, so the servers' addresses are never public.
hosting.notes: Region and instance details are in the private infrastructure repo.

inTransit.internal: Between Cloudflare and our servers, traffic is encrypted and the certificate is verified. Inside our private network, the application connects to its database over TLS.

atRest.method: AES-256, keys managed by the cloud provider
AES-256, keys managed by the cloud provider

backups.frequency: continuously, with point-in-time restore, plus a nightly export of each database
backups.restoreTesting: every quarter we restore a backup into a separate environment and check it

dataLifecycle.export: You can export all of your notes as Markdown at any time from your account settings.
dataLifecycle.retention: We keep billing records for as long as tax law requires.

accessControl.leastPrivilege: Only the people who operate {{product.name}} can reach production systems, and only through an audited gateway.
accessControl.customerDataAccess: We look at your data only when you ask us to, to keep the service running, or when the law requires it.
accessControl.personnel: Everyone with access signs a confidentiality agreement.
accessControl.gap: Access to production is reviewed when people join or leave, but not yet on a fixed schedule.

certifications.name: PCI DSS SAQ A
certifications.scope: The payment page, which is hosted by our payment processor
certifications.gap: The first self-assessment is scheduled for next quarter.

securityOverview.title: Security overview
securityOverview.description: How we keep {{product.name}} and your data secure.
securityOverview.intro: Your notes are yours, and keeping them safe is our first job. This page says what we do, and where we are not there yet.

practices.title: Redundancy
practices.statement: The database runs with a standby in a second data center that takes over automatically if the primary fails.

practices.title: Access is logged
practices.statement: Every administrative session and every sign-in is recorded in a security event log.

practices.title: Security updates
practices.statement: Operating system security updates install automatically. Application dependencies are checked for known vulnerabilities on every change.

practices.title: Network protection
practices.statement: Our servers accept web traffic only from Cloudflare, and administrative access only from approved addresses.

practices.title: Secure development
practices.statement: Every change is reviewed and tested before it is released, and the same release runs in a staging environment before production.

practices.title: Process isolation
practices.statement: The application runs as an unprivileged user in a restricted sandbox.

practices.title: Security monitoring
practices.statement: Security events from the application are collected in one place.
practices.gap: Alerts on suspicious activity are being set up; today the events are reviewed by hand.

practices.title: Abuse protection
practices.statement: Sign-in and sign-up are rate limited to slow down password guessing.

practices.title: Data centers
practices.statement: We run no servers of our own. Our cloud provider's data centers are guarded, access-controlled and independently audited.

practices.title: Payment processing
practices.statement: Card details go straight to our payment processor; they never touch our servers.

practices.title: Vulnerability reports
practices.statement: We welcome reports from security researchers. See our [security response page]({{doc.security-response}}).

practices.title: Penetration testing
practices.gap: We have not yet had an independent penetration test. The first is planned before we offer team plans.

sections.title: Audits and certifications
sections.outro: {{org.name}} itself has not completed an independent audit, and this page is a self-assessment.

sections.title: Known risks
sections.intro: One shared host runs several products; a kernel compromise would reach all of them.

sections.title: Reporting a concern
sections.intro: See our [security response page]({{doc.security-response}}) to report a vulnerability or an incident.

securityResponse.title: Security response
securityResponse.description: How to report a security problem in {{product.name}}.
securityResponse.intro: If you have found a security problem in {{product.name}}, we want to hear about it.

channels.purpose: For anything that is not urgent or sensitive

process: We confirm the problem and assess its severity, and keep you informed.
We fix it. We do not disclose an issue until it is fixed.
We publish a note about the fix and, if you wish, credit you.
outOfScope: Social engineering of our staff or customers
Reports from automated scanners without a demonstrated impact
securityResponse.safeHarbor: We will not take legal action against research done in good faith that follows this policy, avoids harm to customers and their data, and gives us time to fix the problem before it is disclosed.

subprocessors.title: Subprocessors
subprocessors.description: The third parties that process personal data for {{product.name}}.
subprocessors.intro: We use a small number of third parties to run {{product.name}}. Each is bound by a data processing agreement.

subprocessors.name: Example Mail
subprocessors.gap: Replacing our current email provider next month.

dataHandling.title: Data handling
dataHandling.description: Where your data is stored, how long we keep it, and how it is deleted.

practices.title: International transfers
practices.statement: If you are outside the United States, your data is transferred to and stored in the United States under Standard Contractual Clauses.

incidentResponse.title: Incident response
incidentResponse.description: How we handle security incidents and tell you about them.
process: **Detect.** Security events and alerts reach the on-call engineer.
**Contain.** We stop the incident from spreading, revoking credentials and isolating systems as needed.
**Notify.** We tell affected customers, as described above.
**Recover and learn.** We restore service, and write up what happened and what we changed.
incidentResponse.drills: We rehearse restoring from backup every quarter.

history.title: Breach history
history.statement: To our knowledge, {{product.name}} has never had a data breach.

availability.title: Availability
availability.noCommitment: We do not offer a service-level agreement. We work to keep {{product.name}} available and publish its status.
